issues.title: CSV import/export rules are inconsistent with NULL vs empty-string round-tripping
issues.evidence: NULL" placeholder; distinct from empty string
leaving it empty saves empty string
Empty unquoted fields → NULL; empty quoted fields (`\"\"`) → empty string.
open in PapaParse; all values round-trip correctly
issues.recommendation: Specify a lossless CSV encoding rule for empty strings vs NULL. Concrete option: always export empty strings as quoted empty fields (`""`) and export NULL as empty unquoted fields. Add this explicitly under
and ensure the exporter enforces it. If you want a user-togglable behavior, add an export option, but the default must satisfy the round-trip E2E claim.
issues.acceptanceTest:
E2E (amend US-009):
1) Create table with one TEXT column.
2) Insert two rows: one with NULL, one with empty string.
3) Export to CSV.
4) Assert the NULL row column is an empty unquoted field, and the empty-string row column is `""`.
5) Re-import into a fresh table and verify via SQL: one row is NULL and one is empty string (and not swapped).

issues.title: 100MB goal lacks measurable time/memory thresholds and “no crash” definition
issues.evidence: . None define a time budget for 100MB, a memory ceiling, or what
issues.recommendation: Turn the 100MB requirement into explicit, testable targets: (1) time-to-open and time-to-first-interaction thresholds for 100MB on the baseline environment, (2) a memory ceiling (e.g., JS heap/process RSS upper bound) or at least a max multiplier (e.g., <2.5× DB size in memory), and (3) an operational definition of
(tab reload, browser OOM kill, >N seconds unresponsive). Align these thresholds across Goals, Performance Targets, and Success Metrics so they don’t drift.
issues.acceptanceTest:
Perf test checklist (CI-friendly):
1) Playwright loads 100MB fixture; measure `performance.mark` from drop/open to sidebar populated and first query runnable.
2) Assert time under the defined threshold.
3) Collect memory signal (Chrome `performance.memory` or Playwright tracing + documented proxy) and assert under ceiling.
4) Assert the page remains responsive (no long task > X ms for Y seconds) and no crashes/reloads occurred.

issues.title: SQL editor execution semantics are unclear (single vs multi-statement, transactions, multi-results)
issues.evidence: and describes outputs for SELECT vs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, plus
but does not specify what happens when the editor runs multiple statements, mixed statement types, or partial failure mid-script.
issues.recommendation:
Decide and document one of these explicit behaviors for v1:
A) Single-statement execution only (block multiple statements with a clear error), OR
B) Script execution (split on semicolons with SQLite-aware parsing) with defined result handling.
If (B), specify transaction policy (wrap entire script in a transaction by default and rollback on error, or execute per-statement) and how UI displays multiple result sets (tabs, last SELECT only, etc.). Update US-005 acceptance criteria and add E2E covering both a success multi-statement script and a mid-script error rollback behavior.
issues.acceptanceTest:
E2E (new/updated US-005):
1) Paste script: `BEGIN; INSERT INTO t(x) VALUES (1); SELECT count(*) FROM t; COMMIT;` -> Verify INSERT affected row count is shown and SELECT result set renders correctly.
2) Paste script with error after a write: `BEGIN; INSERT INTO t(x) VALUES (2); SELECT * FROM non_existent; COMMIT;` -> Verify error is shown with correct line number AND (per chosen policy) the INSERT is rolled back (count unchanged) if using atomic script transactions.

issues.title: Table rebuild “preserve indexes/FKs/triggers” promise lacks verifiable acceptance coverage
issues.evidence: but the only E2E listed checks:
—which does not validate indexes, triggers, FKs, or rollback correctness.
issues.recommendation: Expand US-003 acceptance criteria to include explicit post-apply verification for: indexes (`PRAGMA index_list` + `PRAGMA index_info`), triggers (`sqlite_master` entries), and foreign keys (`PRAGMA foreign_key_list`). Add a negative-path test that forces rebuild failure (e.g., introducing a NOT NULL constraint or CHECK violation during copy) and verifies the database remains unchanged (schema + data).
issues.acceptanceTest:
E2E (add to US-003):
1) Create table A with an index, a trigger, and a FK from another table referencing A.
2) Perform a rebuild operation (drop column / rename column).
3) Assert: row count unchanged; `sqlite_master` still contains the trigger; `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` still contains expected FK; `PRAGMA index_list/index_info` still match.
4) Force a rebuild failure and assert the DB schema/data are identical to pre-operation snapshot (e.g., compare `sqlite_master` + row counts + checksum query).

issues.title: ERD E2E FK-count acceptance is ambiguous and likely not implementable as written
issues.evidence: — the SQL contains `...` and `pragma_foreign_key_list` is table-scoped, so there’s no defined way to compute the expected total FK edge count for the whole DB from this statement.
issues.recommendation: Replace the ambiguous E2E evidence with an explicit, DB-wide expected-FK computation and a clear UI mapping. Example: define expected edges as the sum of `count(*)` over `pragma_foreign_key_list(table_name)` for all non-internal tables, and define UI edges as one edge per FK entry (or per column mapping). Put the exact SQL (or algorithm) into the acceptance criteria so test authors can implement it deterministically.
issues.acceptanceTest:
E2E (updated US-004):
1) Compute expected FK count with a deterministic query/algorithm defined in the PRD (e.g., iterate tables from `sqlite_master` and sum `pragma_foreign_key_list`).
2) Load Chinook fixture.
3) Assert rendered ERD edge count equals expected count (DOM query for edges).
4) Assert at least one known FK (e.g., a specific table/column pair from Chinook) is present as an edge label/source/target.
